newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices return to gains on low inflows.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices return to gains on low inflows.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Thursday returned to gains after a modest correction, dealers said.
Consumer buying as well as retail interest remained slow but restricted inflows from mills and a shortage of ready stock lifted prices.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by eight rupees at 1,418/1,440 rupees per quintal while M-30 rose by 5/10 rupees at 1,460/1,495 rupees.

"Inflows of sugar from mills to the Bombay market remained at a low ebb as most of the millers have already sold out their allotted quantity of sugar from the free sale quota of the current month," one broker said.
Mill delivery trading also remained nominal on scattered offerings by the millers and sugar mill delivery was nominally quoted at 1,360/1,370 rupees per quintal.

Overall volumes were thin as traders were awaiting state-wise allocation of sugar out of the free sale quota of 800,000 tonnes announced for June. Quota for current month is also 800,000 tonnes against 750,000 released during last month.
